ledger.x: c. 1450 BC: the kingdom of Ugarit stands on the Syrian coast. The page says only that the polity 'was at its height c. 1450 to c. 1185 BC'; it gives no founding year (the city is attested in the Mari archive c. 1765 BC and had been a vassal of Yamhad, undated), so the start is a bridging judgment.

c. 1345 BC (bridged): Ugarit becomes a Hittite vassal. 'Niqmaddu II reigned c. 1350 - c. 1315 BC. Ugarit became a Hittite vassal, first under a viceroy at Karkemis'; the Niqmaddu II page calls him 'a vassal ruler of Suppiluliuma I of Hatti' and dates Suppiluliuma's Mitanni campaigns c. 1350-1345 BC, without dating the…

c. 1185 BC: the Hittite vassalage ends with the destruction of Ugarit. The infobox date of the destruction is c. 1185 BC; the destruction table c. 1190 BC; radiocarbon and eclipse evidence 1192-1190 BC; Ammurapi (c. 1215 to 1180 BC) is the last king and a contemporary of Suppiluliuma II.

c. 1185 BC: Ugarit is destroyed. 'The city may have been destroyed around 1192-1190 BC' (Ammurapi page); the Ugarit page's infobox gives c. 1185 BC and says it 'would become one of the many states of the ancient Near East that were destroyed or abandoned'; Ammurapi's letters speak of 'the seven ships of the enemy that…

wars.name: Revolt of Mukish, Nuhashshe and Niya against Ugarit and Hatti
wars.outcome: Itur-Addu of Mukish, Addu-nirari of Nuhashshe and Agi-Teshub of Niya 'turned hostile'; Suppiluliuma I's treaty with Niqmaddu II (CTH 46) records it.

wars.name: Destruction of Ugarit by the Sea Peoples

certainty.note: The kingdom is a coastal strip of about 2,000 km2; no treaty line is drawn on any page opened.
